national_baseline: Among Tier A manuals that mention extended detention, site-wide water-quality volume depth is most often cited at 1 inch (n=30, median 1, range 0.37–1.61 inches), reflecting jurisdiction-level sizing rather than a single facility storage depth. Site-wide maximum drawdown time clusters at 72 hours as the mode with a median of 48 hours (n=36, range 4–120 hours). Seasonal high water table separation for pond-type BMPs is frequently 24 inches at the mode but 36 inches at the median (n=36, range 12–120 inches), again as site-wide context. Where manuals specify extended-detention drain or drawdown time for the practice itself, the mode is 24 hours with median 40 hours (n=25, range 24–72 hours). Basin geometry guidance is thin but when present favors a length-to-width ratio of 2 (n=19, median 2, range 0.3–3). These figures describe extracted manual language, not an adopted national standard.

regional_modifiers.title: Cold climate and shorter drawdown windows
regional_modifiers.text: Several northern and mountain jurisdictions pair extended detention with shorter site-wide maximum drawdown or practice drain times than the 72-hour site-wide mode—for example 24-hour caps at flagstaff-az and seattle-wa for site-wide max drawdown, and 24-hour ed_drain_time_hours at ak-state, mn-state-2008, ma-state-draft, md-state, and vt-state. Minnesota site-wide WQv depth is 1.25 inches (minneapolis-mn, ia-state-ch1 proxy context) versus the 1-inch mode elsewhere.

regional_modifiers.title: Coastal and high water table — tighter SHWT separation
regional_modifiers.text: Site-wide seasonal high water table separation drops to 12 inches in several manuals (chesapeake-va, raleigh-nc, maine-manual, mt-deq8, nj-state chapter proxy), below the 24-inch mode. Texas coastal sizing includes 48-inch separation at houston-tx and tx-edwards-rg348 where cited.

regional_modifiers.title: Karst-sensitive groundwater (Edwards-related citations)
regional_modifiers.text: Texas Edwards-related guidance in the matrix lists 48-inch SHWT separation, 48-hour ed_drain_time_hours, and a length-to-width ratio of 1 at tx-edwards-rg348—distinct from the 2:1 mode where geometry is specified.

regional_modifiers.title: Arid West — shallow WQv and mixed drawdown
regional_modifiers.text: Las Vegas site-wide WQv depth is 0.37 inches with 72-hour max drawdown and 24-inch SHWT separation (las-vegas-nv). Denver site-wide WQv is 0.6 inches (denver-co). Albuquerque site-wide max drawdown is 96 hours (albuquerque-nm-gsi). Practice ed_drain_time at las-vegas-nv is 24 hours.

open_issues: Roughly half of Tier A manuals lack extractable numerics for key site-wide fields (WQv depth missing in 45 of 76; max drawdown and SHWT each missing in 38 of 76). Extended-detention-specific ed_drain_time_hours is documented in only 25 of 60 mentioning manuals (missing 32), and length-to-width ratio in only 19 (missing 40), so geometry and facility drain-time baselines are not yet established numerically at national scale. Site-wide drawdown ranges from 4 hours (fl-fsesci-tier1) to 120 hours (ms-state-vol2), and SHWT from 12 to 120 inches (san-diego-ca), indicating strong regional divergence not fully captured in a single temperate default. Several values rely on chapter_proxy extractions (ia-state-ch1, de-wet-ponds-draft, nj-state, va-state). Whether site-wide WQv and drawdown limits map one-to-one to extended detention basin design versus broader stormwater programs remains an interpretive gap for synthesis.
matrix_summary: For extended detention in Tier A manuals (60 of 76 mention the practice): site-wide WQv depth mode 1 inch (n=30, 0.37–1.61); site-wide max drawdown mode 72 h, median 48 h (n=36, 4–120); site-wide SHWT separation mode 24 in., median 36 in. (n=36, 12–120); practice ed_drain_time mode 24 h, median 40 h (n=25, 24–72); length-to-width ratio mode and median 2 (n=19, 0.3–3).
